agree.reason: The candid admission about the ratings and the refund and update commitments would reassure a wary backer who has lost money before, but the vague budget, the missing game title and creator name, and the omitted launch-week reviewer video leave real gaps for this reader.

honest.reason: The 'proven hit' claim is tempered by an open disclosure that the raters had met the creator, but 'more than twice the backers it needs have already raised their hands' treats email signups as near-backers, and 'refused to send it out until it was right' adds colour the facts don't support.

works_the_facts.reason: The 572-backer and 'fewer than half of signups' figures are correct and well framed, but the draft never works out the budget: $17,400 for printing, $9 shipping and about $2,800 in fees against $28,000, which leaves roughly $2,650 at goal. It also hand-waves 'the rest of the goal' and never explains 1,500 copies against 572 backers.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is signups against backers needed. There is no clear picture of what happens if the goal is missed or how this risk compares with the reader's other options.

qualification.reason: The refund pledge names a month (November 2027), a threshold (three months late) and a consequence (a full refund on request), but it doesn't state the actual cutoff date (February 2028) or the campaign dates.

objections.reason: The first-time-creator objection is met head-on with commitments, but the burned backer's central question, whether $28,000 really covers printing, shipping and fees, goes unanswered, and the independent reviewer video that would answer 'only friends rated it' is left out.

fit.reason: It is a crowdfunding pitch of about 500 words with sensible sections, but it never names the game (Lantern Winter) or the creator, which a campaign pitch needs.
